title: Punyakoti, the Truthful Cow
director: claude-opus-5-5 (authored in Claude Code, same rules as scripts/audio/direct.ts)

cast.name: Punyakoti
cast.description: Gentle mother cow, calm, dignified, loving

cast.name: Arbhuta the tiger
cast.description: Old hungry tiger, menacing, later ashamed

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [warmly] Welcome to LitBridge, where stories cross languages. Today's story comes from the Kannada tradition. It comes from Govina Haadu, the song of the cow, still sung to children in Karnataka. It is called... Punyakoti.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In a village at the foot of the Karnataka hills lived a cowherd named Kalinga. In his herd was a cow called Punyakoti.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the forest above lived a tiger named Arbhuta. He was old and hungry. One evening, he leapt out in front of Punyakoti as she grazed apart from the others.

lines.speaker: punyakoti
lines.text: [calm] Wait. I have a calf at home who has not been fed. Let me go and give her milk one last time, and say goodbye. Then I will come back... and you can eat me.

lines.speaker: tiger
lines.text: [mocking laugh] Ha! What prey ever came back?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But something in her eyes made him curious. And he let her go.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [tender] At home, Punyakoti fed her calf, and gave her all the advice a mother can give in one evening.

lines.speaker: punyakoti
lines.text: [softly] Stay near the herd, my little one. Be kind to the other mothers. And never wander near the forest alone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The other cows begged her not to go back.

lines.speaker: punyakoti
lines.text: [firm, gentle] A promise is a promise. If I break it, what is the use of the life I save?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At dawn, she walked back up the hill and stood before the tiger.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [long pause] Arbhuta looked at her for a long time. He had killed many creatures, but he had never met one who walked back to her death to keep her word.

lines.speaker: tiger
lines.text: [ashamed, low] You are my sister... and I am a sinner. How could I eat a creature like you?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [solemn] Overcome by shame, he leapt from the cliff. And Punyakoti went home to her calf.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [gently] The song of Punyakoti is still a child's first lesson in Karnataka about keeping one's word. Thank you for listening to LitBridge.
